spec_match.rationale: The disjoint-breakpoints comma rule and the @media analogy are spec-accurate and the container setup is valid, but the page's match verdicts are JS width arithmetic, not the spec behaviour — in this pre-150 browser they claim the comma rule is APPLYING while the rendered card proves it is not.

interactive.rationale: The drag-to-resize stage with a real ResizeObserver-driven width readout is genuine, but drag is the only way to drive the core demo — no slider or button alternative — and the generated 'scenario focus' panel is navigation, not feature interaction.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises drag-resize, live status badges and the <250px/>500px blue-border OR rule, which is exactly what the page implements.

edge_cases.rationale: No capability detection: in a browser without comma-separated container queries the rule is parser-dropped and the pills/live-code still report it applying (screenshot shows pill on + 'APPLYING' with a black-bordered card).

references.rationale: No chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952 link anywhere on the page — see-also has only sibling links, violating invariant 3.

conformance.rationale: The shared feature suite asserts real parse/CSSOM contracts and honestly fails 4 of 5 here.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Verified via headless Chromium 141 cloud fallback (full-page screenshot + DOM, not chrome-devtools-mcp): at 708px Rule 1's row layout applies, Rule 2's blue styling does not despite pill/code claiming it — drag-resize itself was not driven.

telemetry_health.rationale: Baseline injected telemetry only; the pill/rule state transitions emit no events.

design_system.rationale: Variables throughout; walkthrough and pill 'on' states set background and color together.

accessibility.rationale: The walkthrough panel has aria-live and real buttons, but the primary interaction (CSS resize handle) is not keyboard-operable or touch-reliable, match pills have no live region, and active-scenario state is not exposed via aria-pressed.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Layout wraps cleanly at 1280px headless, but on touch devices the CSS resize corner is effectively unusable, leaving the core demo undrivable on mobile; the ≈360px class was not exercised.

openQuestions.title: Derive rule-match state from rendered styles, not width arithmetic
openQuestions.detail: The ResizeObserver callback computes r1/r2 from the measured width and reports them as rule matches. In this Chromium 141 session the live code block printed 'rule result: ✓ APPLYING' while the card border stayed black because the comma rule was dropped by the parser. Read back getComputedStyle(.demo-card-cq).borderColor / flexDirection so the pills and annotated code reflect reality, and surface a 'comma rules unsupported — requires Chrome 150+' notice when the observed style disagrees (CSS.supports('(min-width:1px),(min-height:1px)') inside @container probing, as the conformance suite does).

openQuestions.title: Add the missing ChromeStatus reference link
openQuestions.detail: Invariant 3: every page must cite chromestatus.com/feature/6196591858941952 — it is the self-heal anchor. This page has none.

openQuestions.title: Give the resize interaction a keyboard/touch-operable alternative
openQuestions.detail: The only way to change the container width is the CSS resize:horizontal corner, which keyboard users cannot operate and touch users struggle with. Add a width slider or preset-width buttons (as sibling concepts do) wired to the same stage so the core demonstration works on every input modality.

openQuestions.title: Announce match-state changes
openQuestions.detail: The rule pills flip between on/off with colour and text but no aria-live region, so the demo's entire output is silent for screen-reader users. Mirror the pill state into a polite live region (the walkthrough output already shows the pattern).

openQuestions.title: Update the 'Chrome 149' card tag to the real ship milestone
openQuestions.detail: The lineage note records this feature shipping in Chrome 150; the card-tag badge and 'Chrome 149+' code comment should say 150 (or 'Chrome 150+, listed in 149').

summary: Reviewed with the headless-Chromium-141 cloud fallback (not chrome-devtools-mcp): full-page screenshot + DOM of /v149/comma-separated-container-queries/multi-condition-explorer/ and the feature /conformance/ route (HTTP 200; panel 1 pass / 4 fail / 0 blocked). The stage, ResizeObserver width readout and annotated live code are a good explorer shape, and Rule 1 (plain min-width) demonstrably applies — but the screenshot caught the comma rule being reported as APPLYING while the rendered card stayed black, the page carries no ChromeStatus link, and the sole resize interaction excludes keyboard and touch users. Drag-resize was not driven headless.
